# plan/ — Havemind planning package (generated by the `loopstart` skill)

This folder closes out Havemind from its current state (`plans/002-pilot-tasks.md`, T001-T033)
to a successful seven-day pilot on `sapserver` and the Phase 8 gates. Generated per the
`loopstart` skill (`~/Downloads/SKILL (1).md`), reviewed by a critic agent, fixes applied.

## How to get started (TL;DR)

1. Check the environment: `node --version` (22 LTS), `gh --version`, the `ponytail` and
   `caveman` plugins installed (or remove the first 2 lines of the block in
   `10-MASTER-PROMPT.md`).
2. Check that `ssh sapserver` works (Tailscale active on the MacBook).
3. Open a new Claude Code session in the `havemind` repo.
4. Paste the block from `10-MASTER-PROMPT.md` (the ` ``` ` fences) in full.
5. After Phase F0 the agent will suggest `/remote-control` — enable it if you want a preview
   from your phone during the long loop.

## What you (the user) provide along the way

- **SRV-02**: the decision on where the Restic backup lands (USB / NAS / Backblaze B2) —
  without this, SRV-03 is stuck.
- Confirmation of the two one-off test-vault setup before the F8 gate (names/machines).
- A time window for the seven-day pilot (when you can react to `Conflict`/`Offline`).
- **SRV-07**: a physical trip into the BIOS at the next sapserver restart — the agent can't
  do this remotely (no IPMI/BMC on this board).
- The `sudo` password on `sapserver`, typed manually in the terminal when the agent asks for
  it — never handed to the agent to store.
- Approval to `push` to the remote repository, once the backlog reaches a stage where that
  makes sense (the agent commits locally without asking within the loop, but never pushes
  without confirmation).

## Open decisions

1. **Scope of rule 8 (agent access to sapserver) vs `plans/001-technical-plan.md` §14
   "Ask first: deploy or change privileged configuration on sapserver."** The user explicitly
   asked for standing permission for the building agent to modify `sapserver` without asking
   every time. Resolution: rule 8 (`01-zasady-i-slownik.md`) narrows the canon's meaning of
   "privileged configuration" to ONLY the items in rule 9 (sudo, Funnel, the docker group,
   irreversible operations, publishing the repo, changing the encryption model). Everything
   outside that list — routine `docker compose up`, creating Compose files, configuring
   Tailscale Serve — the agent does on its own. This is a deliberate, documented narrowing of
   one point of the canon by the user, not a defect in the package.
2. **Local `git commit` without asking within the `/loop`**, despite the user's global
   instruction "don't commit without asking" (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). Resolution: the user
   accepted the orchestrator+subagent architecture from the `loopstart` skill, which requires
   one commit per issue without interrupting the loop to ask. The exception covers ONLY a local
   commit in the Havemind repo within this loop — `push` still always requires asking. Recorded
   explicitly in rule 9.
3. **Phase numbering**: the package uses `F0-F9` (the `loopstart` methodology), not
   `Phase 0-8` from `plans/001-technical-plan.md`. Mapping: `F7`≈Polish/hardening, `F8`≈the
   pilot gate (canon Phase 7), `F9`≈canon Phase 8 (follow-up). The critic found an original
   naming collision (`Fk+1`/`Fn` as letters, not numbers) — fixed by renumbering to numeric
   values across all files.
4. **SRV-07 (BIOS power-loss autostart)** can't be performed or verified remotely by the
   agent (the ASRock Z370 board has no IPMI/BMC) — marked `user-decision`, the agent returns
   this as a request in this phase's first report instead of entering a loop of 3 failed
   attempts.
5. **Second critic round**: the critic (a general-purpose agent) found structural gaps
   (missing issue F7-03, phase-numbering collision, inconsistent AC). All were applied directly
   in files 01, 08, 11 by the planning session instead of through a second full critic-agent
   round — a deliberate shortcut, because the fixes were mechanical and mapped 1:1 to the
   findings (they didn't require a new assessment). If new structural gaps show up after
   further backlog changes, run a full second critic round instead of relying on this shortcut.

## Kickoff (to paste to the user / for you to run now)

A new Claude Code session in the `havemind` repo, in this order:
1. Read `CLAUDE.md` (repo).
2. Read `plan/01-zasady-i-slownik.md` → `plan/02-fundamenty.md` → the rest of `plan/0X-*.md`
   in numeric order.
3. Verify the environment: `node --version`, `ssh sapserver` (connection test), the
   ponytail/caveman plugins.
4. Paste the block from `plan/10-MASTER-PROMPT.md` and start the `/loop` from the START
   section.
5. Checkpoints: after F0 (foundation green), after F3 (first working onboarding —
   take a screenshot), after F7-02 + SRV-06 (first deploy worth showing) — show the result to
   the user before continuing to the F8 gate.
